chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
title: Sarah asks to sing with his trio; Mr. Dikes refuses her
summary: Looking for a job for the trio with Sarah Vaughan, he is insulted by a Maryland club owner who will not hire her and never works for him again.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Anyway, I was very fortunate... When Tommy came back to Washington, I got Tommy and Chester, and we formed this trio. While I was forming the trio, one day I happened to get a call from Sarah Vaughan. She just called me to say hello. She says, "What are you doing?" I said, "I'm putting a trio together." She says, "Oh yeah, fine." I said, "What are you
doing?" She said, "I'm not doing anything. I have a home in New Jersey." She said, "Could i sing with the trio?" I said, "Of course you can! Soon as I can find a job for us."

So I go out to try and find a job. And there was a club here, out in Maryland, on the outskirts of Sea Pleasant, Maryland, called Dikes. The fellow's name was Mr. Dikes. He had a place out there where he had this club, and he had gambling, he even had a little hotel out there, and he had a place for the summer, an outdoor place that they called the Stockade, just because he had a big fence around it, just like a stockade. He played big bands out there and all of that. I went out to see him, because for a couple of weeks, a few weeks before I had gotten this job at the Caverns, back where I had this little band, I had played with a band out there at his Stockade, a band that had this fellow Georgetown in it -- Danny Brashears that I talked about earlier. Which was a nice little band, but it didn't stay together.

So I knew Mr. Dikes, so he was the first one that I went to, to talk to about a job. He said, "Oh yeah, John. You can get a job here any time you like. Who have you got in your group?" I said, "Well, I got Tommy Potter, the bass player that worked with me out here. And I have Chester Brown. You know him. He used to work with Tommy Miles' band." He said, "Oh yeah, I know him." And I said, "And I've got a vocalist."

He said, "Oh good! Who's the vocalist?" I said, "I've got a girl named Sarah Vaughan." "Sarah Vaughan? Who is that?" "You remember when I was playing with the Eckstine band last year and we played the Howard Theatre, and you came by, you came backstage to see Billy?" He said, "Yeah, I remember." I said, "Well, it's the girl who sang with the band?" He said, "What? That little black bitch?" He said, "John, I wouldn't hire her singing in my toilet." He said, "Man, bring me a pretty woman. Bring me somebody who look like Lena Horne or something, and I'll give you a job." I never told Sarah this. But I was very hurt by it, and I was really mad with him. And I never went back to ask him for the job, I never tried to find anything... As a matter of fact, I never worked for him again.
